exposure: Management of placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) with a standardized Multidisciplinary Approach to the Placenta Service (MAPS) protocol
Management of placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) without a standardized Multidisciplinary Approach to the Placenta Service (MAPS) protocol
cohort: Patients who underwent cesarean hysterectomy (c-hyst) for suspected placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) from 2012 to 2022 at a single tertiary care center
finding: An evidence-informed Multidisciplinary Approach to the Placenta Service (MAPS) protocol was associated with decreased complication rates, estimated blood loss greater than 1 liter, ICU admission rates, and length of hospitalization in women undergoing cesarean hysterectomy for suspected placenta accreta spectrum.
